conformal.note: each detector's model tail was replaced by its rank in that detector's own burn-in distribution, frozen at the boundary: p_conf = (1 + #{i : p_i <= p}) / (n + 1), which is super-uniform under exchangeability whether or not the null holds. A conformal p-value cannot fall below its floor, so events past the burn-in tail tie there and are ordered by model_log_p, which is the same combination over the detectors' own p-values and is a tie-break only

coverage.entity_population: source users matching U*@ (human accounts); see DATA.md burn-in section
coverage.statement: corpus days 7.00 to 9.00 scored (burn-in days 0 to 7.00)

dependence.note: cov(-2 ln P_i, -2 ln P_j) estimated directly from burn-in co-evaluations and frozen at the boundary, per the rule §8.2 applies to the partition: a quantity used to score an event may not have been fitted on it. The Kost-McDermott value implied by the same correlation is recorded beside each direct estimate for comparison, but the direct estimate is what (19) consumed

combination.method: Fisher (18) with Brown's correction (19); the covariance is the direct sample covariance of -2 ln P per detector pair, measured on burn-in only and frozen at the boundary

entity_sample.note: a deterministic sample of ENTITIES, not of events: per-entity histories are left whole, and only whole entities are dropped. Every labelled entity is kept regardless of the sample, so the labelled share of this corpus is inflated relative to the full population and a detection rate measured here is NOT comparable to one measured on the full population. The co-occurrence graph and the population marginals are built from the retained entities only
entity_sample.selector: FNV-1a 64 of the entity identifier, modulo N, equals zero

anomaly_categories.definition: structural properties of an event relative to the history it was scored against, derived from verdict evidence and NOT from which detector produced the smallest p-value; a partition defined by our own detectors would flatter the framework by construction

fisher_over_the_day.score: sum of -2 ln P over the entity's events, descending

entity_days.note: one record per (entity, corpus day). The framework's premise is that the unit of analysis is the individual, while the alert budget is spent on events; these are the same evidence aggregated to the unit the premise names, and to the unit an analyst actually triages. Neither score is a calibrated p-value at entity scope: an entity's own events are not independent

seeds.note: no stochastic component in the scoring path (R4)
